children: , China's e-commerce and cloud-computing giant, rose approximately 0.7% to $109.42 Friday despite allegations that operators associated with the company improperly extracted Claude's reasoning capabilities. Reuters said Alibaba did not immediately respond to its request for comment. The market's reaction was clear: investors noticed the accusation, but they did not rush for the exit.

Anthropic's company-authored investigation linked more than 151 million exchanges between May and July to what it described as an unauthorized distillation campaign designed to improve Qwen models. Activity reportedly approached three million exchanges per day at its peak and ran through thousands of fraudulent accounts. These are Anthropic's claims, not findings established by a court or regulatora crucial distinction while Alibaba remains publicly silent.

Alibaba's latest results showed AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue climbing 45% to 48.44 billion yuan, roughly 18% of total revenue. The image places Alibaba's $109.42 share price 8.68% below its $119.82 GF Value, suggesting modest upside to that estimate. But the bigger investor question is not mathematical: Alibaba must show that the technology powering its fast-growing AI business was built on a credible and defensible foundation.

title: Alibaba Gains as Anthropic Alleges 151 Million Illicit Exchanges
